summary: Discovery complete for Ledgerly: PRD with 10 requirements (REQ-001..REQ-010; 6 must, 4 should) covering auth, clients, line-item invoices, send-ready view, paid/unpaid tracking, and the outstanding-totals dashboard. Scope excludes email sending, payments, multi-user, multi-currency, and analytics; 8 items deferred to v2. Two personas and 5 numeric success metrics defined.
assumptions: 'Send-ready' means a presentation-complete printable/shareable invoice view; no email sending in v1 (carried from intake, restated as riskiest assumption).
Two invoice statuses only (unpaid/paid); no draft/sent/overdue states in v1.
Paid invoices are locked from editing; user must revert to unpaid to edit (REQ-008), protecting paid-total integrity.
Clients with invoices cannot be deleted in v1; only zero-invoice clients can.
Password reset and email verification deferred because v1 has no outbound email.
Dashboard 'total paid (period)' interpreted as current calendar month.
Sequential per-account invoice numbering (INV-0001 style) inferred as standard invoicing hygiene.

questions.text: Brief fixes db=sqlite (local demo) with a public-facing SaaS ambition later; confirm the auth/session and data-access design does not bake in sqlite-only assumptions that block a v2 Postgres move.

summary: Next.js 16.3 + TS 7 + Prisma 7 on SQLite via driver adapter (Postgres-portable per ADR-001, resolving Q-001); 5 entities (User, Session, Client, Invoice, InvoiceLineItem); 16 operations across 10 paths in OpenAPI 3.1 with envelope, 8-code error registry, cookie auth, and fixed-25 pagination on the invoice list; 5 ADRs.
assumptions: Q-001 resolved in ADR-001: cuid2 app-generated ids, no raw SQL, string statuses, integer numerics, and DB-backed sessions keep the v2 Postgres move to an adapter swap + data copy.
Money is integer cents and quantity integer thousandths end-to-end (ADR-003); rounding is round-half-up per line then sum.
Paid invoices cannot be DELETED either (PRD only locks editing) — same INVOICE_PAID_LOCKED rule; revert to unpaid first.
Invoice detail embeds the client as a live reference (no snapshot), satisfying REQ-002's 'edits reflect on existing invoices'.
Status toggle endpoint is idempotent; paid->paid does not move paidDate.
Pagination exists only on the invoice list (page size fixed 25); clients and dashboard recents are unpaginated per PRD thresholds.
Dashboard 'paid this month' and all date-only defaults use UTC calendar days.
Password minimum length 8; emails lowercased for uniqueness; signin returns one INVALID_CREDENTIALS code for both bad email and bad password (no enumeration).
Invoice display number INV- + zero-pad to 4 grows naturally past 9999 (INV-10000).
Client list sorted name-ascending; invoice lists sorted issueDate desc then number desc.

Auth: signup(201)/signin(200) set the ledgerly_session cookie (HttpOnly; SameSite=lax; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; opaque 256-bit base64url token, Session row keyed by its SHA-256, 30-day sliding expiry refreshed at most once/24h); signout deletes the row and clears the cookie; me returns the user; duplicate email 409 EMAIL_TAKEN, wrong password AND unknown email both 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS with no session row, guarded routes without cookie 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; DB stores argon2id PHC hashes ($argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$...). Clients: all five operations at /api/clients and /api/clients/{clientId}; list name-ascending with invoiceCount; empty name 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with field details; PATCH null clears a field, {} rejected (minProperties 1); foreign-account and unknown ids both 404 NOT_FOUND; delete with invoices 409 CLIENT_HAS_INVOICES, zero-invoice delete returns {deleted:true}. typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0 after all writes; dev server killed and test rows removed from data/ledgerly.db.
assumptions: Signout is guarded like every non-signup/signin endpoint (contract: only signup/signin are exceptions): no cookie at all -> 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; WITH a cookie it is idempotent - a token whose row is already gone still returns 200 {signedOut:true} and clears the cookie.
Auth runs before body validation on every guarded route, so a signed-out caller always gets 401, never a 400 revealing payload shape.

Sliding expiry is implemented as: refresh expiresAt to now+30d when the last refresh is >=24h old (derived as expiresAt - 30d); expired rows are hard-deleted on lookup per the data-model lifecycle sweep.
Signin emails are trimmed + lowercased before lookup (contract only says lowercased); signup stores the normalized form.

EMAIL_TAKEN is detected by catching the unique-constraint violation (P2002) from the create transaction rather than a pre-check, so concurrent signups cannot race past it; the error-code check is structural to keep the concrete Prisma client out of services.
Client list sort is SQLite's default BINARY collation via Prisma orderBy name asc (case-sensitive); contract only says name-ascending and Prisma offers no collation control on SQLite.
PATCH /clients treats an absent key as untouched and an explicit null as clear, matching ClientPatchInput; a JSON undefined cannot occur so the distinction is safe.

The vitest integration tests named in T-004/T-005 acceptance do not exist yet (no test infra task has run); acceptance was proven by exercising every listed behavior with curl against the dev server plus direct SQLite inspection for the argon2 hash and session-row deletion. questions.text: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL must be set at BUILD time, not runtime. /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and every canonical are statically prerendered, so the origin is baked into the build output - a runtime-only value silently ships a sitemap and canonicals pointing at http://localhost:3000. Proven both ways in this session. This needs to be a Docker build arg promoted to ENV in the builder stage plus an entry in .oma/06-devops/env.template. I did not edit the Dockerfile or env.template - your territory. The fallback is http://localhost:3000 so dev, e2e and a fresh clone are unaffected.

Two filed items, both with the measurement that motivates them. (1) There is not a single <a> element on either public page - fetched and counted, zero anchors on /signup and zero on /signin. The Sign in / Create account toggle is <button>s calling history.replaceState, so a crawler landing on /signin has no crawlable path to /signup and the sitemap is the only way either is discoverable from the other. Needs a real anchor beside the toggle. (2) /signup ships 1016 KB raw / 292 KB gzipped of JavaScript for an email field, a password field and a button. One chunk is 454.6 KB raw (45% of the total) and contains the zod runtime, framer-motion, AND the whole schema barrel including invoice symbols (displayNumber, totalCents) the auth screen never uses - because auth-screen.tsx imports from the '@/shared' barrel, which re-exports every schema, and zod schemas are constructed at module top level so nothing tree-shakes. Importing from '@/shared/schemas/auth' is the one-line fix; measure before and after rather than assuming the saving.

framer-motion is on the public entry page to buy exactly two things: the auth card's enter.default fade and the mode toggle's move.default indicator slide. If those are its only use there, a CSS transition honouring prefers-reduced-motion gets the identical result at zero library cost on the one page every new visitor loads first. This would change the mechanism, not the frozen motion-spec values - durations and easings stay exactly as specified. Your call before anyone touches it.

The single highest-leverage SEO change here is not metadata, it is that / currently 307s to /dashboard and there is no public page describing the product. Anyone arriving from a link, a post or a search result lands on a login form with no explanation of what they are logging into. oma-marketer has already written and claim-checked the copy in landing-copy.md; what is missing is the route. Do you want that built as a v1.1 task?
